title: Microsoft Graph OAuth Business Write (Ultrawork PLAN)
goal: Implement delegated Microsoft Graph OAuth business-write support for customer-facing OpenCode and AnythingLLM MCP usage while forbidding send, delete, raw Graph, and application-permission access.
targetUsers: All acquired customers who use the Microsoft Graph MCP integration through OpenCode and/or AnythingLLM
constraints: Use delegated Microsoft user permissions only
Do not store tokens or secrets in OpenCode or AnythingLLM config
Do not expose direct email send, email delete, calendar delete, or raw Graph passthrough tools
Use a customer-facing MCP server name without unnecessary Pros branding, or document a compatibility alias
If Microsoft Graph implementation behavior is unclear or fails, read official Microsoft documentation before guessing
Attachment support must use extension allowlist, MIME validation, and conservative size limits
Attachments allowed: pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, odt, ods, odp, txt, csv, tsv, png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp
Attachments forbidden: archives, binaries/executables, scripts, source code, macro Office files
mustHave: OAuth setup and status for business-write-safe delegated scopes
OpenCode and AnythingLLM command-only MCP configuration
Calendar event create/update/invite with delegated shared calendar targets
Email draft create/update with delegated shared mailbox targets
Server-side confirmation gates for write operations
Tests for policy, forbidden operations, status states, attachments, shared targets, and MCP tools
Customer-facing documentation and runtime workflow updates
forbidden: Archive, binary, executable, script, source-code, and macro-office attachments

findings.scopes: MICROSOFT_GRAPH_SCOPES (microsoft-oauth.ts:100-110) is read-only: openid, profile, offline_access, User.Read, Mail.Read, Calendars.Read, Files.Read, Team.ReadBasic.All, Channel.ReadBasic.All. Must add Mail.ReadWrite and Calendars.ReadWrite (replacing Calendars.Read).
findings.status: getGraphStatus (microsoft-graph.ts:368-402) returns a single 'ready' status after a /me probe. It reads stored scopes but does NOT derive a capability tier. Tier logic (needs-auth, ready-read, ready-business-write-safe, limited, needs-reauth, needs-admin-consent) must be added.
findings.mcpServerName: microsoftGraphMcpServer (mcp-microsoft-graph.ts:20-170) is named 'pros-mcp-microsoft-graph'. Referenced in mcp-evaluations.ts (2 evaluation questions) and mcp-servers.test.ts (server name assertion at line 17-18). Rename must update all three plus any client-config command builder.
findings.mcpTools: Current MCP surface has 5 read tools: graph_status, graph_search_mail, graph_list_calendar, graph_search_files, graph_read_excel_range. All are readOnlyHint. 6 new write tools must be added with confirmation gates and destructiveHint:false.
findings.toolInterface: ProsMcpTool (mcp-common.ts:15-25) takes (input, runtime). Confirmation must be enforced via input schema (confirmationStatus field) checked in handler before any Graph write call.
findings.registry: BRIDGE_PROVIDERS (integration-registry.ts:2-134) microsoft-graph provider has 4 read capabilities (mail.read, calendar.read, files.read, excel.readRange). Must add business-write-safe capabilities (mail.draftWrite, calendar.write) with scopes Mail.ReadWrite / Calendars.ReadWrite.
findings.clientConfig: McpInclude type (mcp-client-config.ts:11) is currently 'hubspot' only. Must widen to 'hubspot' | 'microsoft-graph'. McpClient (opencode | anythingllm) already supports both. Configure functions currently HubSpot-focused via expectedOpenCodeHubSpotEntry / expectedAnythingLlmHubSpotEntry patterns; Graph entries need analogous command-only builders.
findings.graphModule: microsoft-graph.ts exposes read functions + graphGet helper + validators (validateQuery, validateCalendarRange, validateA1Range, validLimit). Write functions (createCalendarEvent, updateCalendarEvent, inviteAttendees, createDraft, updateDraft, addDraftAttachment) and a shared-target resolver must be added. A graphPost/graphPatch helper analogous to graphGet is needed.
findings.tests: No dedicated *graph*.test.ts exists. Graph coverage lives in mcp-servers.test.ts. Related tests: integrations.test.ts, cli.test.ts, mcp-client-config.test.ts. New safety/write tests need a home (dedicated microsoft-graph*.test.ts recommended).

decisionLog.rationale: The work spans OAuth, Graph API, MCP tools, client configuration, tests, and docs with cross-boundary contracts.

decisionLog.decision: Use delegated Microsoft user permissions only
decisionLog.rationale: The user wants rights at the level of the signed-in user and no application-wide mailbox/calendar permissions.

decisionLog.decision: Forbid send, delete, and raw Graph operations
decisionLog.rationale: Direct sends and deletions are explicitly disallowed, and raw Graph would bypass safety policy.

decisionLog.decision: Research official Microsoft documentation when blocked
decisionLog.rationale: Graph behavior for drafts, attachments, shared resources, and recurrence can be subtle and must not be guessed.

decisionLog.decision: Add graphPost/graphPatch helpers instead of a generic graphRequest passthrough
decisionLog.rationale: A generic passthrough would violate the no-raw-Graph constraint; typed write helpers keep the surface safe while remaining simple.

decisionLog.decision: Canonical MCP server name 'microsoft-graph' with documented compatibility alias
decisionLog.rationale: Customer-facing naming should avoid unnecessary Pros branding; alias preserves existing released configs without breaking them.
